Also need to test initialiseParse, parse, runParser, processStartTag overloads, processEndTag, currentElement. We can mock Tokeniser and Token to control flow. Since Tokeniser is not easily mockable without external libs, we could subclass TreeBuilder and override tokeniser with a stub that returns predetermined tokens. Since tokeniser is package-private class, but we can create subclass in same package org.jsoup.parser to access protected fields. We'll create a TestTreeBuilder extends TreeBuilder with simple implementations: defaultSettings returns new ParseSettings (assume class exists). process method will just store last token processed and return true. Assume Tokeniser is not final and has a constructor with CharacterReader and ParseErrorList. We'll create a subclass FakeTokeniser extends Tokeniser and override read() to return tokens from a queue. We need to create Token objects: Token.StartTag, Token.EndTag, Token.TokenType.EOF. Assuming Token class structure exists; we can create new Token.StartTag().name("a") etc. Use them.

2. testProcessStartTagReusesToken: Ensure that when currentToken is start (i.e., we set builder.currentToken = builder.start), calling processStartTag("p") creates new Token.StartTag not using start token; we can check that token passed to process is not same instance as start (by overriding process to capture token). We'll set builder.currentToken = builder.start and call processStartTag("p") and assert captured token != builder.start.

3. testProcessStartTagWithAttributes: pass Attributes (maybe create new Attributes()) and verify token has name and attrs set. We can capture token and inspect.

4. testProcessEndTagSimilarReuse.

5. testCurrentElement: push an Element onto stack and verify currentElement returns it; when stack empty returns null.

6. testParseRunsParserAndReturnsDoc: Provide a FakeTokeniser that returns a StartTag token then EOF. The process implementation will push an element onto stack when receives StartTag, and maybe track token types. After parse, doc should be not null and baseUri matches.

However we can indirectly cause it by calling processStartTag which sets currentToken? Not. currentToken is only used for error tracking; not set in TreeBuilder. - builder.currentToken = startToken;

- call builder.processStartTag("div"); capture token passed to process (via override). Ensure captured token != startToken.
